summary: Anthropic opened a research preview of the Model Hardware Standard (MHS), a shared specification and driver protocol letting Claude and other AI agents safely operate laboratory and manufacturing hardware such as liquid handlers, robotic arms and microscopes, tested with partners including Genentech and University of Washington labs.

mechanisms.reason: The standard is explicitly designed to let agents run autonomous, round-the-clock multi-device workflows in place of manual specialist operation.
mechanisms.quote: MHS also helps researchers and engineers more readily orchestrate autonomous, round-the-clock experiments and workflows, with agents able to reason through each step in an experiment, update parameters in real time, and, in some cases, recover from hardware errors without intervention.

practices.reason: Describes a concrete architecture (standardized drivers, MCP/CLI/API control, chaining commands into deterministic code files) with a stated integration-time gain, but it is a narrow research preview limited to physical-lab hardware rather than a general software stack.
practices.quote: MHS reduces this integration work to hours or minutes.

practices.reason: Introduces a new standardized interface (drivers, tags, MCP access) that any agent harness would need to integrate against to control hardware, though it is still an early access-gated preview.
practices.quote: MHS works with any device that has a programmable interface. It is also model-agnostic, and any agent harness can access it using standard protocols, such as the Model Context Protocol .

practices.reason: The lab states an intent to build safety evaluations and best practices for agents operating physical equipment, but no method or instrument is yet described.
practices.quote: We’re sharing an early version of MHS with partners across science, robotics, electronics, and manufacturing so we can collaborate to build safety evaluations and develop best practices for AI systems operating physical equipment, ahead of making the standard open source.
